summary: Controlled administrative review of bench screen suitability for the Vehicle ladder and Excipient compatibility screen work. Balance checks, dilution record traceability and recipe card reconciliation are confirmed complete. Three actions are closed and one is carried into the next bench cycle.

title_block.title: Bench Screen Suitability: Administrative Review
title_block.subtitle: Vehicle ladder and Excipient compatibility screen

blocks.p: This review confirms that the screen suitability records for the Vehicle ladder and Excipient compatibility screen work packages are complete, traceable and consistent with the recipe cards in use. It covers bench sheets issued from 09/23/2024 to 10/25/2024. It is an administrative check of the records and does not re-assess the formulation conclusions drawn from the screens.

Screen suitability is recorded on each bench sheet before a formulation set is compounded. A sheet that fails a check stays open until the failure is explained on the sheet itself, not in a separate email.
The review was carried out under the transition rules. The local master still applies for this year, and project and accession numbers are cited as they were issued.

Balance checks were reviewed for every bench sheet in scope. Each check is recorded with the date, the operator's initials, the reference mass used and the result against the tolerance printed on the sheet. Reference masses trace to the calibration log kept by Sample Management.

list: Every bench sheet carries a balance check entry for the day of weighing.
Two entries were made on a neighboring balance while the usual instrument was out of service. The sheets name the balance used, so the record is complete.
No check was recorded as passed without a value. Where a value was missing the weighing was repeated and the sheet annotated.

blocks.p: Ashley King confirmed that the balance identifiers on the sheets match the calibration log. No discrepancy was found.

Vehicle ladder dilutions were made from stock solutions expressed in mg/mL. Each dilution step is recorded as its own line on the bench sheet, with the parent stock, the volume transferred and the resulting concentration. A reviewer should be able to rebuild any ladder step from the sheet alone, and this review checked that they can.

Three steps referred to the parent stock by a shorthand label rather than the stock ID. Miguel Serrano added the full stock IDs on 11/05/2024 and initialed the change. The original entries are still legible.

Excipient compatibility screen dilutions follow the same layout. Concentrations are given in mg/mL throughout. Weight percent appears only where a blend is described as a loading, and no mixed-unit entries were found within the screen itself.
Each recipe card used for the screens was compared with the bench sheets that cite it. The table records the outcome for each card.

RC-24-038 carries a note. The card states the blend loading in weight percent, while two bench sheets record the same blend against its mg/mL concentration. The values agree after conversion and the card was not changed, but it now states both units so the next reader does not need to convert.
No bench sheet cites a superseded revision of any card.

rows: Shorthand stock labels on dilution sheets
Full stock IDs added and initialed
Card revised to state mg/mL and weight percent
Use of neighboring balance not in calibration log
Entry to be added to the calibration log

blocks.p: The open action does not affect the screens already closed. It is carried into the next bench cycle so the log is complete before the next screen starts.

The screen suitability records for the Vehicle ladder and Excipient compatibility screen work are complete and traceable, and the recipe cards reconcile with the bench sheets. The review finds no reason to hold the screens. The formulation set can move to its development note on the same basis.
